title: Thawing and Seeding Frozen Cells
author: Kenneth Schackart
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.3rcgm2w

steps.title: Thaw Cells
steps.instruction: Thaw the cells by suspending the cryotube in a 37 °C water bath until completely thawed, but no longer than necessary.

steps.title: Transfer Cell Suspension
steps.instruction: Within a biosafety cabinet, transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube using a 1000 μL pipette.

steps.title: Initial Medium Addition
steps.instruction: Slowly add warmed cell culture medium to the cell suspension to prevent osmotic shock.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL warmed cell culture medium dropwise.
Add an additional 3 mL warmed cell culture medium slowly.

steps.title: Remove Supernatant
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant from the tube, taking care not to disturb the cell pellet.

substeps.instruction: Remove the bulk of the supernatant with a serological pipet.
Remove the remainder with a 1000 μL pipette.

steps.title: Resuspend Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in warmed cell culture media.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL warmed cell culture media to the cell pellet and let it rest for about 2 minutes.
Gently pipette mix the cell pellet into the solution.
Add an additional 7 mL warmed cell culture media (or 3 mL for T-25 flasks).

steps.title: Seed Cells into Flask
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension to the tissue culture flask using a serological pipet.

steps.title: Label and Incubate Flask
steps.instruction: Label the flask and place it in the incubator.

substeps.instruction: Label the flask with Cell line, Passage number, Date, and Your initials.
Transfer the flask to the CO2 incubator.

steps.title: Update Inventory
steps.instruction: Remove the used vial from the frozen storage inventory.
